english_title: Counterexample 2.4: Counterexample in the Summation Version
statement_en:
Let $\Omega=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$, let $\mu$ be counting measure, and let $\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ be the power set. Define on $\Omega^2$ the function
$$f(i,j)=\begin{cases}1&\text{ if }i=j \\ -1&\text{ if }i=j+1\\ 0&\text{ otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
Interpret
$$\int_{\Omega^2}f(i,j)d(\mu\times \mu) =\sum_{i,j\in\Omega}f(i,j),$$
and show that this is not absolutely summable because
$$\sum_{i,j\in\Omega}|f(i,j)|$$
diverges. Therefore Fubini's theorem does not apply, and the two iterated sums differ:
$$\su
final_code:
import Mathlib

abbrev Omega := {n : ℕ // 1 ≤ n}

def f (i j : Omega) : ℝ :=
  if i.1 = j.1 then 1 else if i.1 = j.1 + 1 then -1 else 0

theorem countingMeasureFubiniCounterexample :
    ¬ Summable (fun p : Omega × Omega => |f p.1 p.2|) ∧
      (∑' i : Omega, ∑' j : Omega, f i j) = 1 ∧
      (∑' j : Omega, ∑' i : Omega, f i j) = 0 := by
  sorry
